items.title: feat(context): add native source records and evidence-backed atoms
items.body:
> **Current naming/source contract, 23 October 2026:** this is The Onlinesourdough Method (OSM). Use Context Architecture for the data/context design; AI Operating Model keeps its name. Production naming is delivered in [PR80](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/80), released v0.30.0. The pre-existing Setup feature preview is preserved separately in [PR81](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/81), not promoted to production. Current implementation paths below use `osm` / `osm-*`; [#76](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/76) tracks remaining rollout. All functional requirements and holds remain; naming delivery does not mean this feature has shipped.

## Problem and result

OSM already has durable Memory metadata and decision reasons. What is missing is a distinct, queryable place for selected session/meeting evidence and derived atoms before they become trusted durable knowledge. Add the smallest native record model that makes those records useful to people and agents, preserving existing Memory and Docs semantics.

Parent: [#68](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/68). Contract dependency: [#69](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/69). Provides the record contract to [#71](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/71), [#72](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/72) and [#73](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/73).

## Default Notion shape

- Reuse an appropriate existing Docs/Meetings destination for captured source records. A new default may use Docs with its existing `Type = Source` view for sessions; meeting notes keep the resolved Meetings destination. Do not create a new Sessions database merely to obtain another view.
- When the selected capture workflow needs atoms and no suitable store exists, create **one small Atoms database** linked to its source records. An existing compatible database/view can implement the same role. This is not a new native Notion `database_type`, and not a replacement or second copy of Memory.
- Keep the source map at source-system/scope level; a captured document is an individual session/meeting. Define the link between those two identities so hundreds of sessions do not become hundreds of dashboard systems.
- Keep source evidence at its owning system when durable accessible references suffice. Store a sanitized source excerpt/export only when that retention is selected. Summaries and atoms link to the exact evidence location; missing full evidence is an explicit limit.

## Minimal semantic contract

Use existing fields with matching meaning; do not force identical names or widen every database. Put searchable/filterable values in native properties, richer provenance/rationale in the page body. Define the default physical schema and views in the Context-owned reference before creation.

| Record | Required meaning | Native representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source record | Stable origin identity scoped to provider/account; route; source URL/export reference; original event date if known; capture time; observed source revision if available; summary; completeness/access state | Existing Docs/Meetings title, Key, Source/Date where semantically compatible; add only missing properties needed by the selected workflow, with evidence/provenance in body |
| Atom | One independently useful claim; stable key; origin relation plus evidence locator; kind; original date inherited/recorded; topic/project where useful; state | Small Atoms database: descriptive title/claim, Key, Source relation, Kind, Status and relevant date/topic properties; body holds exact evidence, uncertainty, derivation and reason |
| Promotion | Durable Memory/Doc/Skill destination and relationship to originating evidence | Link/reference to the actual owning record; no parallel live task or repeated profile |

Define two separate identities: a stable source-item Key (provider/account/route + original item ID) and an observed revision/processed revision. An edit is not an unrelated new source. Atom Keys identify their source/revision and logical claim; rerunning extraction first reconciles existing claims rather than treating a differently worded summary as new knowledge. Native Created time can represent initial capture only when that meaning holds; migration must preserve the original captured time separately.

Define minimal lifecycle meanings, mapped to existing compatible properties: active, changed/incomplete, unavailable (unconfirmed access/fetch failure), confirmed deleted/revoked, and forgotten by the owner. Apply recorded exclusions before collection. Retain only the minimal non-content identity/exclusion marker needed to prevent reimport after forgetting, subject to the owner's deletion policy; never keep the forgotten claim in a tombstone. Where a marker itself must be removed, the route must be excluded/disabled or an equivalent upstream exclusion must prevent reimport.

Keep explicit derivation links from atom to evidence and from atom to promoted destinations. Prefer native relation(s) to the actual destination types, or stable URLs plus an indexed relation where necessary; do not assume one Notion relation can target arbitrary databases. Existing Memory schema remains intact. A dependent claim with no remaining valid evidence is marked for review under the standing write policy and excluded from current answers pending resolution; independent corroboration is evaluated rather than deleted. A bad extraction batch can be identified by its receipt/route and extraction time and retracted without deleting original evidence or later human corrections.

An atom can be a reported fact, decision, constraint, lesson, or verified fix. Mark extraction vs human/source confirmation explicitly. Do not invent confidence percentages, reasons, authors or dates. Preserve the exact original error/command when useful and safely scoped; an attempted command is not a proven fix.

Memory's native `Source` remains the creating client and `Last updated by` the editing client; original evidence stays separate. Do not conflate Docs `Source`/`Date` with Memory's native meanings. `Imported`/capture time is not source date or proof of currency. Existing Decision `Reason and evidence` content remains.

Provide useful Recent, Needs review and By source/project views over the same records, not duplicated databases. Space/filters organize content but grant no access. Derived records must not be shared more broadly than the approved source/retention policy allows.

## Source owners and acceptance

Context's `references/home-contract.md`, `references/notion/schema-and-templates.md`, `references/notion/operating.md` and provider equivalents own the schema. This issue also owns the parent-listed deliberate capture-policy update; Capture and Maintain Context link to it. Extend existing templates and migration/recovery procedures only where needed. Optional file-home records do not require an `AIOS_FORMAT` change unless readers actually need a new mandatory format; preserve unknown files under the existing contract.

- [ ] Create a synthetic source record and related atoms through the actual supported Notion connection; property-filter/view/search finds a useful atom and follows it to evidence without loading the full transcript.
- [ ] Reuse a populated compatible Docs/Meetings/Memory setup without renaming native semantics or changing existing IDs/permissions/content. Unchanged replay creates no new database or atom.
- [ ] Old source imported today retains its old/unknown source date; explicit decision, uncertain statement and failed attempt remain distinguishable. A planted secret is absent from persisted excerpts, atoms and summaries.
- [ ] Corrected/superseded/unavailable evidence can be represented and excluded from ordinary current answers without erasing useful history. Record migration/additive setup has readback and a bounded recovery path.
- [ ] The same roles work in the existing managed-file home using ordinary files/frontmatter or an existing index. No mandatory external index or new general storage abstraction is introduced.
- [ ] Verify a new write by direct ID/property query even while ordinary search indexing lags. Preserve evidence/exclusion markers and original capture times across an authorized home move. A forgotten record is not recreated by the next intake; a bad batch is recoverable without erasing later owner edits.

This issue does not claim every existing Memory row is complete, does not import owner data, and does not redesign all Notion databases. Native capability checks precede claiming support on a specific plan.

items.title: Different results in console output and generated files
items.body:
Hello @kkartas 👋 ,

I do obtain different outputs concerning the running of your `example.py` file and it seems strange to me. 
1. I ran `python3 example.py` and I obtained the following output:

```
🔄 Generating synthetic test data...
✅ Generated 1000 rows of test data → customer_test_data.csv

📊 Sample of generated data:
   customer_id               name  ... customer_tier  registration_date
0         4782  Jacqueline Cooper  ...          Gold         2024-12-31
1         1133        Juan Nelson  ...        Silver         2024-06-02
2         4656       Ryan Jenkins  ...        Bronze         2021-06-10
3         6445         Janet Yang  ...        Silver         2024-04-06
4         1802    Brittany Meyers  ...        Silver         2023-10-02

[5 rows x 6 columns]

🔍 Validating generated data...
❌ Validation failed with 2 errors

🧪 Testing validation with corrupted data...
❌ Corrupted data validation: 5 errors found
   1. {'type': 'invalid_type', 'column': 'customer_tier', 'row': 1, 'message': "Value 'Invalid' is not of type 'category'"}
   2. {'type': 'range_violation', 'column': 'customer_id', 'row': 0, 'message': "Value '-1' is below minimum 1"}
   3. {'type': 'duplicate_value', 'column': 'email', 'row': 405, 'message': "Duplicate value 'xmiller@example.com' in unique column 'email'"}
📄 Detailed error report saved to: validation_errors.csv

🎉 Example completed! Key benefits demonstrated:
   • Single schema drives both generation and validation
   • Realistic data with Faker integration
   • Comprehensive validation with detailed reporting
   • Perfect synchronization between test data and validation rules
```

* I have the file `customer_test_data.csv` and it looks correct regarding the input schema. OK.
* In the output, it says "Validation failed with 2 errors". 
    * Is this normal? 
    * If so, where is the detailed report of these two errors?
* For the corrupted data, the output says "Corrupted data validation: 5 errors found"
    * However, in the detailed report `validation_errors.csv`, I obtain only 4 lines : 
      * For customer 1133 : invalid_type: Value 'Invalid' is not of type 'category'; invalid_category: Value 'Invalid' is not in allowed categories ['Bronze', 'Silver', 'Gold', 'Platinum'] 
      * For customer -1 : range_violation: Value '-1' is below minimum 1
      * For customer 811 : duplicate_value: Duplicate value '[xmiller@example.com](mailto:xmiller@example.com)' in unique column 'email'
      * For customer 1562 : duplicate_value: Duplicate value '[xmiller@example.com](mailto:xmiller@example.com)' in unique column 'email'
    * Can you clarify which output is correct?

items.title: GAS-ROADMAP-002 — Competitor-informed evergreen capability roadmap
items.body:
Status: OWNER-DIRECTED / EVERGREEN INTERNAL R&D PROGRAM
Owner: G.A.S. Product Orchestrator (current repo instructions: Product ORCH2)
Portfolio parent: LowcountryDigitalWorks/business-operations#280
Priority: P1 long-running internal product capability
Cost Class: $0 / included / low-cost first
External commercialization: service-first and separately validated; internal product development is NOT blocked on buyer demand

# GAS-ROADMAP-002 — Competitor-informed evergreen capability roadmap

## Owner direction — 2026-09-29

Lowcountry Digital Works will continue developing G.A.S. Engine as a long-running internal Search / SEO / AI-visibility intelligence product even when immediate customer demand is not yet proven.

The commercial gate and the internal R&D gate are intentionally different:
- Internal R&D may continue because LDW itself benefits from a stronger search/visibility operating system and the owner explicitly wants this as an ongoing strategic development project.
- External managed service may use accepted G.A.S. capabilities through business-operations #280 and continue buyer/service validation.
- External SaaS/customer software remains separately gated by real demand, support/security/privacy burden, customer ownership, and commercial evidence.

Do not use lack of current buyer proof as a reason to freeze useful internal capability development.
Do not use this direction as permission to build a large multi-tenant SaaS, crawler, dashboard stack, custom auth, paid data warehouse, or autonomous publishing system without a separate gate.

## North star

Build a provider-neutral evidence and decision-support system that helps LDW repeatedly answer:
1. What changed?
2. Where is visibility improving or degrading?
3. Why is the change likely happening?
4. Which opportunities are material enough to act on?
5. What bounded action should be proposed?
6. What changed after the action?
7. What should remain monitored?

Lifecycle:
OBSERVE -> NORMALIZE -> COMPARE -> CORRELATE -> DETECT -> PRIORITIZE -> RECOMMEND -> HUMAN/OWNER APPROVAL WHEN REQUIRED -> ACT THROUGH SEPARATELY AUTHORIZED PATH -> REMEASURE -> REPORT OUTCOME

## Competitive-research method

Perform a deep capability-by-capability competitor review before each material G.A.S. expansion.
Do NOT clone vendors or copy proprietary implementations.

For every capability domain:
1. identify the best current specialists / OSS / major-platform features;
2. document the user problem they solve;
3. document inputs, outputs, cadence, and decision model;
4. identify what is commodity sensing vs differentiated interpretation/workflow;
5. choose BUILD / INTEGRATE / CONFIGURE / WATCH / DO NOT PURSUE;
6. estimate recurring cost, support burden, privacy/security burden, and customer-data implications;
7. define the smallest internal proof using LDW-owned/public-safe evidence;
8. implement only after the Product Orchestrator freezes a bounded release.

## Capability domains to research

### A. Search Console analytics / Google search intelligence
References: GSC Wizard, Google Search Console native API/export, SEOTesting-class experiment systems.
Candidate capabilities: striking-distance/page-poaching opportunities; query/page decay; CTR underperformance; cannibalization; brand/non-brand segmentation; content/topic grouping; date-window comparisons; URL inspection/indexing health; anomaly/change-point signals; annotations and before/after measurement.

### B. Query intent / page-focus / content architecture
References: GSC Wizard query-shape analysis; MarketMuse/Clearscope/Surfer/Frase/InLinks; major SEO-suite keyword/topic clustering.
Candidate capabilities: detect one URL serving materially different intent clusters; distinguish consolidation vs split-page opportunities; page/query-cluster mapping; content-gap and supporting-topic evidence; internal-link target suggestions.
Owner-supplied 2026-09-28 GSC Wizard email is design evidence: reverse cannibalization can identify one page collecting unrelated query clusters; split only when each new page can become a real unique page; keep the original URL for its primary intent; compare SERPs/competitors before declaring intents distinct.

### C. Multi-engine indexing/crawl triangulation
References: Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools/AI Performance, Yandex Webmaster, IndexNow.
Candidate capabilities: compare indexing/crawl state across engines; distinguish site-wide technical breakage from engine-specific behavior; preserve per-engine freshness/coverage windows; detect inconsistent canonical/index states; record IndexNow submission/indexing observations without treating Bing/Yandex ranking as a proxy for Google.

### D. Technical SEO / site quality
References: WQT, SiteOne, Lighthouse, Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, Ahrefs Site Audit, Semrush Site Audit.
Candidate G.A.S. role: consume normalized technical evidence; preserve semantic magnitudes/trends/provenance; correlate technical changes with search/visibility outcomes; do not rebuild a crawler.

### E. AI / answer-engine visibility
References: ZeroRank plus Profound/Peec/Scrunch/Otterly-class platforms and Bing Copilot visibility.
Candidate capabilities: prompt/brand visibility trends; citation/source coverage; source-URL concentration; competitive mention gaps; visibility change after bounded site/content changes; provenance and prompt-cohort consistency.

### F. Rank / SERP / competitor intelligence
References: Ahrefs, Semrush, SE Ranking, Moz, DataForSEO-class providers.
Candidate stance: avoid building a rank crawler; use native/free/vendor data only where it materially improves decisions; preserve source/freshness/coverage and do not blend unlike rank universes into one proprietary score.

### G. Local SEO / local business visibility
References: Google Business Profile; BrightLocal/Whitespark/Local Falcon-class tools.
Candidate capabilities: GBP completeness/visibility evidence; local query/landing-page opportunities; review/reputation linkage where separately authorized; local-pack/grid data only when a low-cost source proves useful.

### H. Links / authority / internal linking
References: Ahrefs/Majestic/Moz; GSC links data; crawler-derived internal-link graph.
Candidate capabilities: internal-link opportunity scoring from existing site graph + search demand; backlink change evidence only if an affordable authoritative source exists; no custom internet-scale backlink crawler.

### I. SEO experimentation / annotations / outcomes
References: SEOTesting; Search Console annotations/change logs; statistical experimentation systems.
Candidate capabilities: change annotations; bounded pre/post cohorts; same-source remeasurement; outcome confidence/not-yet-measurable state; avoid causal claims when only correlation is supported.

### J. Reporting / operator workflow
References: GSC Wizard reports/MCP; Looker Studio/AgencyAnalytics-class reporting; accepted G.A.S. operator case view.
Candidate capabilities: deterministic compact metrics before LLM interpretation; source/freshness/unit/window attached to every derived fact; maximum-three-priority customer summary; deeper operator detail separate from customer view; MCP/read-only API only when repeated operator friction justifies it.

## Cross-cutting design principles learned from GSC Wizard
1. Heavy arithmetic/aggregation happens deterministically before model interpretation.
2. Models receive compact finished metrics, not huge raw Search Console row dumps.
3. Every signal carries source, period, freshness, coverage, units, filters and provenance.
4. Preserve API-specific reporting lag instead of manufacturing zeroes for missing days.
5. Filters such as brand/content group/topic cluster are typed dimensions, not ad hoc prose.
6. Connected-provider errors distinguish permission/property/verification problems from generic reconnect advice.
7. Multi-engine evidence is comparative diagnosis, not score blending.
8. Recommendations are grounded in measured evidence and rechecked after implementation.

## Immediate research + roadmap output
Create a living competitor matrix in the repository with: capability; user job/problem; leading products/platforms; useful patterns; commodity vs differentiated; BUILD/INTEGRATE/WATCH/SKIP; data source/credential implications; recurring cost; privacy/security; smallest proof; candidate G.A.S. release.

Then propose the next three bounded releases, prioritizing reusable internal value over UI breadth.

## Initial likely release sequence — hypothesis until Product Orchestrator freezes it

### Candidate 0.10 — Search Analytics Signal Pack
Pure/deterministic analytics over normalized GSC-like evidence: trend windows; striking-distance; decay; CTR opportunity; cannibalization; brand/non-brand grouping; explicit data-window/freshness semantics. No provider networking required for the first mechanism proof.

### Candidate 0.11 — Intent / Page-Focus Analysis
Provider-neutral page/query-cluster representation and split/consolidate opportunity evidence. No autonomous content generation. No SERP scraping unless separately authorized and justified.

### Candidate 0.12 — Multi-Engine Index Diagnostics
Provider-neutral index/crawl state model that can compare Google/Bing/Yandex-style evidence and classify broad site issue, engine-specific issue, or coverage uncertainty. No rank-score blending.

Later candidates may cover AI-visibility correlation, internal linking, experiment/annotation intelligence, and richer operator workflows.

## Implementation authority
This issue authorizes competitor research and roadmap definition.
Each software release still requires current-main reconciliation, exact release contract, smallest proof, branch/PR, deterministic tests, security/privacy review, independent review, and Product Orchestrator acceptance before merge/next release.
No direct production/customer mutation follows from a G.A.S. recommendation.

## Automation relationship
Automation & Agent Operations owns provider/event ingestion, read-only sensor collection paths, scheduling/event triggers, executor routing, generated evidence handoff, and operational observability.
G.A.S. Product Orchestrator owns domain contracts, normalized semantic model, deterministic analysis, recommendation/measurement/outcome logic, release roadmap, and product acceptance.
business-operations #280 remains the managed-service/commercial application gate.
